query_text: can parathyroid disease cause neck pain

content.text:
Yes—**parathyroid disease can be associated with pain**, but **true “neck pain” is not one of the most typical symptoms**.

**Most common parathyroid problem:** hyperparathyroidism, where too much parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium. It more commonly causes **bone or joint pain, muscle weakness, fatigue, kidney stones, constipation/abdominal symptoms, mood or memory changes**, and frequent urination. ([mayoclinic.org](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hyperparathyroidism/symptoms-causes/syc-20356194?utm_source=openai))

Because the parathyroid glands sit in the **front/base of the neck near the thyroid**, a large parathyroid growth, thyroid-related issue, or—rarely—parathyroid cancer could cause a **neck lump, pressure, swallowing changes, hoarseness, or localized discomfort**, but this is less common. UCLA advises contacting a clinician if you feel a **lump in the neck** or have symptoms of high calcium. ([uclahealth.org](https://www.uclahealth.org/medical-services/surgery/endocrine-surgery/patient-resources/patient-education/endocrine-surgery-encyclopedia/hyperparathyroidism?utm_source=openai))

If you have **persistent neck pain**, other causes are often more likely—muscle strain, cervical spine/disc problems, swollen lymph nodes, thyroid disease, infection, etc. Parathyroid disease is usually checked with blood tests: **calcium, PTH, vitamin D, kidney function**, sometimes urine calcium.

**Get urgent care now** if neck pain comes with trouble breathing/swallowing, high fever, severe headache/stiff neck, chest pain, new weakness/numbness, or rapidly enlarging neck swelling.

If you tell me your symptoms, calcium/PTH results if you have them, and where the neck pain is—front of neck vs back/side—I can help you think through what to ask your doctor.
